newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER SHOWCASE-HOW BORO COULD HAVE DONE WITH CAPTAIN MARVEL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-HOW BORO COULD HAVE DONE WITH CAPTAIN MARVEL.

text.p: If Middlesbrough manager Bryan Robson could have turned the clock back 10 years and signed himself as the player he was at his peak, Middlesbrough could probably have escaped relegation this season.

Instead Robson, who is still officially Middlesbrough's player-manager, had to grapple with an ever-tightening noose and relegation's trapdoor. How he could have done with a midfield warrior like himself battling and scrapping for every loose ball, every inch of ground gained.

Captain Marvel, as he was known in his long career at Manchester United, ploughed past tackle after tackle, ran from one penalty box to the other and was often in the right place at the right time to bang home a crucial goal.

Instead he made just one, fleeting appearance all season. Now 40 years old, the game he played at Arsenal on New Year's Day was probably the last of a career which brought him 90 England caps, two league titles and three F.A. Cup wins with Manchester United and the European Cup Winners Cup in 1991.

Now he will try and join the select band of men who have captained and also managed an F.A. Cup winning side, but even if Middlesbrough do beat Chelsea and win the Cup for the first time in their 121-year history, the victory will be a bitter-sweet one.
Middlesbrough might yet be playing in European football next season, but they will also be playing back in the first division just two years after Robson led them into the premier league.

He said: "This is the first time I have ever experienced relegation in my career and it's not something I am enjoying. I said a few months ago that I fully expected to get the sack if we went down and, while the future is still uncertain, I welcome the chance to learn from this season's mistakes and take us back up again.
"But I have no regrets about the team I produced, no regrets about signing Juninho or Emerson or Fabrizio Ravanelli or any of the other foreign players.
"I went into management to produce teams that entertain because it was what I had grown up with. I always had the utmost respect for the Brazilian teams I had played against and many of the players.

"I don't deny that Emerson and Ravanelli took some time to settle in, but there is no question about their quality. If either their talent or their attitude was under scrutiny why is it that I have a queue of people trying to buy them."
Robson believes that reaching two cup finals this season seriously weakened Middlesbrough's attempt to stay up after they ran into a period of bad form in mid-seasn.
"We had injuries, but the two long cup runs affected us as well. The players were tired, sluggish, especially at the end of the season playing four matches in nine days.

"Professional football is a tough world and I don't expect any favours from anyone. Relegation has shattered everyone at this club, but at least we have the chance of ending the season on a high. It might not be ideal, but it would be better than nothing."

Robson was just three minutes away from securing Middlesbrough's first ever major trophy six weeks ago when they led Leicester 1-0 in the League Cup final at Wembley before fate played the hand that has always denied Middlesbrough a major honour. Leicester equalised with 118 minutes on the clock and went on to win the replay.
So now Middlesbrough face the possibility of not only going down, but also losing two finals in the same season.
Robson the player survived three broken legs in his career, a badly dislocated shoulder and countless other injuries to build his Captain Marvel reputation.

If his side can lift themselves and show that kind of spirit on Saturday, they must be in with a chance. It's the type of occasion Captain Marvel would have relished. He must hope his players feel the same way.
